A. Lithium-7 reacted unexpectedly
B. The tamper was made of Lead instead of Uranium
C. The secondary stage failed to ignite
D. Atmospheric pressure was too high

Answer: Lithium-7 reacted unexpectedly
Detail: Designers assumed only the Lithium-6 isotope would contribute to the fusion process. However, the high-energy neutrons from the fission trigger caused the "inert" Lithium-7 to capture a neutron and decay into tritium, fueling a much larger fusion reaction than calculated.

4. In the Therac-25 accidents, what specific software error led to the massive radiation overdoses?
A. Integer underflow
B. Divide-by-zero error
C. Buffer overflow in the UI
D. Race condition in the control task

Answer: Race condition in the control task
Detail: The bug occurred when a fast-fingered operator corrected an input error in less than eight seconds. This specific timing caused the software to "lose track" of the hardware state, firing a high-power electron beam without the heavy tungsten target in place to convert it to safe X-rays.
